hints.title: Differentiating Set Bit Partitioning
hints.text: The cumulative bitwise xor of all numbers equals the xor of the two unique values. How can a differentiating bit partition the numbers into two isolated groups?

hints.title: Lowest Differing Bit Isolation Invariant
hints.text: Isolating the lowest set bit in the total xor gives a bit where the two target numbers differ, allowing clean two-group partitioning.

hints.title: Two Group Bitwise Accumulation Procedure
hints.text: Xor all elements to get total xor sum. Find the lowest set bit using diff = xor bitwise-and minus xor. Partition all numbers into two groups based on whether this bit is set, accumulating separate xor sums in each group to isolate the two unique numbers.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: input array length or bit count
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Hash tables consume O(N) space, violating the O(1) extra memory constraint.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Two-pass bitwise xor operates in linear O(N) time using O(1) auxiliary variables.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should isolate the differentiating bit with x & -x and handle 32-bit signed overflow in languages like C++.
